messages:
observability-bot: ALERT: hosted-infer p99 gateway latency SLO breached in us-west-2 (window 5m). SLO: 300ms, observed p99: 1.2s. Error spike: 5xx rate up 4x. Link: https://grafana.company/reports/alert/2432100000 :rotating_light:
Ava (SRE): saw it, acking. grabbing traces + logs. any customer-facing incidents yet?
Marta (Support): yes — Customer 'AcmeAI' opened a support ticket ~2m ago: they see repeated 504s and long tail responses on generate endpoint. They attached curl test: `curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"rdw-3b","prompt":"<~1k tokens>"}'` -> 504 after 30s.
Ravi (oncall): oncall here. what's the initial hypothesis? ingress overloaded or model prefetch/cache issue?
Eli (Infra): quick check: edge-proxy upstream 502/504 counts spiked and backend latency for hosted-infer-prefetch queue jumped. I see a pattern where requests with large prompt sizes hit a KV cache-miss, then backend does an expensive prefetch, which times out.
Ava (SRE): can you paste the Loki query you used? want to check trace coverage and any missing spans.
Eli (Infra): Loki query: ```
{job="edge-proxy"} |= "upstream" | json | line_format("${status} ${upstream_host} ${latency_ms}") | sort_desc by latency_ms
```
Results: many 504s reported with upstream_host="hosted-infer-prefetch-02" and latency_ms ~ 30000ms.
Sam (ML Ops): that host is serving a mix of heavy long-context requests and VLLM-backed models; we recently pushed a quantized kernel change on that pool yesterday night. Could be a regression in prefetch/kvcache interaction.
Marta (Support): customer repro attached a short curl loop they used: ```for i in {1..5}; do time curl -s -X POST ...; done``` — each run either returns 200 fast or 504 at ~30s. intermittent. They want to know mitigation ASAP.
Ava (SRE): running trace sampling for a 10m window now. Noticing trace gaps: many incoming requests have no downstream spans from the model runtime — spans drop between edge-proxy -> ingress-router. Possible TCP resets or connection queue backlog.
Ravi (oncall): can we temporarily force-routing of acme's tenant to a different pool (fallback-route) to reduce customer impact? Marta, can you patch their tenant routing to dedicated-fallback-1?
Marta (Support): doing it now via admin console — applied route override for tenant acme-ai -> dedicated-fallback-1. Will monitor.
Eli (Infra): pushed a quick mitigation: scaled up hosted-infer-prefetch pool by +2 instances and lowered prefetch timeout from 30s -> 15s to fail fast. Patch command: ```./infractl scale pool hosted-infer-prefetch --add 2 && ./infractl set-config hosted-infer-prefetch prefetch_timeout_ms=15000```
Sam (ML Ops): noted. Also rolling back the quantized kernel on one canary node to see if error rates drop: `kubectl rollout restart ds/rdw-infer-kernel --selector=canary=true`
Ava (SRE): capture of timeline for postmortem: 1) SLO alert fired 2) support ticket from Acme 3) trace gaps & upstream 504s 4) mitigation: route override + scale + timeout reduction + kernel canary rollback.
Ravi (oncall): after route override, acme's requests appear normal (p99 back to ~220ms). Good. however global SLO still showing elevated p99 due to noise from other tenants hitting the same prefetch pool.
Eli (Infra): creating infra ticket INF-4782 with logs + node IDs. I included the Loki and Jaeger links and the relevant `edge-proxy` snippets.
Marta (Support): customer updated: "Thanks, response improved after your change. Please advise root cause." I'll send preliminary status.
Sam (ML Ops): follow-up action: revert kernel change on the rest of the pool if rollback on canary reduces errors. Also add a prefetch circuit-breaker to short-circuit heavy prompts to fallback models instead of blocking.
Ava (SRE): can someone run the query to list requests with prompt_size > 800 and status >= 500 in the last 15m? want counts.
Eli (Infra): Loki query: ```
{job="edge-proxy"} |= "generate" | json | spath input=body.prompt_size | prompt_size>800 and status>=500 | count_over_time(15m)
```
Count: ~120 failures in 15m across 6 upstream hosts, 78 of which on hosted-infer-prefetch-02/03.
Ravi (oncall): next steps: 1) temporary mitigations (done) 2) infra rolling rollback if canary confirms 3) add circuit-breaker and prefetch timeout change to runbook 4) follow-up postmortem linking INF-4782 and ticket with customer. I'll own the P0 and schedule a 1hr deep-dive.
Ava (SRE): I'll start a perf dashboard pinned to the incident and capture logs/spans. Please drop any traces or unusual logs here.
Marta (Support): summarizing for customer note: "We detected a prefetch-related backend degradation causing intermittent 504s for large prompts. We applied a route override to a fallback pool and scaled the prefetch pool; your requests are back to normal. We're doing a root cause investigation and will follow up." :white_check_mark:
Eli (Infra): logging INF-4782: nodes involved, recent kernel bundle version, and config diffs. ETA initial RCA in 24h.
Sam (ML Ops): adding an eval to reproduce with heavy prompt + cache-warm/cold cycles. will post the script here when ready.
Ava (SRE): thanks team. keep this thread for updates; I'll convert to a postmortem doc once we have the RCA. :memo:
